speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a limp and localized pain but no fever. To begin our assessment, can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and how long you have been experiencing the limp?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful; the left knee pain with a limp but no trauma or fever in a 7-year-old raises concern for a few specific conditions. Can you tell me if the pain wakes him up at night or if it has been present every single day for the last week?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Synovitis of the Left Knee.
